name: Shipwreck on the Seabed
desc: The hulk of a wrecked ship resting on the seabed seen through a column of green water: god-ray shafts spear down from the surface and sway, caustics net the silt, marine snow drifts endlessly and a slow school of fish crosses the gloom; sunlit teal shallows, turbid green murk, a cold moonlit night dive, a false-colour sonar range shade, or a monochrome ink wash.

energy.doc: how much light survives to the bottom — god-ray brightness, caustic strength and overall luminance

scale.doc: wreck size and ray width — from a distant small hulk to a huge hull filling the seabed

density.doc: how much marine snow and how large the fish school

speed.doc: rate of the drift — marine snow fall, ray sweep and the school crossing

haze.doc: water turbidity — how quickly the depths veil out into murk

current.doc: how hard the current sways the kelp, sea whips and marine snow

hue.doc: primary water hue shift off the default blue-green

x.doc: horizontal position of the wreck and bias of the ray sources

y.doc: the surface depth — how much frame is bright water-sky above versus the deep column below

style.doc: aesthetic: teal = sunlit blue-green shallows to a deep navy floor; murk = turbid green harbour water, low visibility; moonlit = cold silver-blue night dive, dark key; sonar = abstracted false-colour range shading, cyan on black; ink = abstracted monochrome dive wash, form from tone

seed.doc: regenerates the ray sources, ribs, kelp, snow and fish

alpha.doc: layer opacity — sinks the whole wreck back behind the performers
